scope: Source/formula, saved native associations and classification review; no optimizer or high-precision numerical rerun
findings: The length variation and negative reciprocal-velocity derivative have consistent factors and signs.
For a sustained face segment, the interpolated normal direction chooses the correct incident cell, with splits at sign changes; coupled opposite endpoint directions are retained.
At a face intersection each normal sign chooses its incident cell. An identically zero normal direction makes the side choice immaterial to the tangential first variation.
Transverse moving-face terms cancel by continuity of slowness. Fixed unperturbed cell crossings suffice in the first-variation integral.
The independent Decimal reciprocal-affine segment integral and binary64 displaced geometry match the saved finite perturbations.
All saved native resource/SEED/FDSN/epoch associations match. Two substantive in-plane decreases are distinguished from two inconclusive near-roundoff normal signs.
limitations: Quadrature evaluates a directional derivative, not a minimization over all feasible joint directions or a global first-arrival certificate.
The frozen helper is used only with subdivisions=1 or4; it does not reject nonpositive subdivision counts and must not be interpreted as validated for those inputs.
80/100-digit consistency is not interval-certified arithmetic. The tiny raw normal signs must not be called demonstrated descent.
No production source, original local flag or optimizer was changed.
